external_entities.name: Colleague
external_entities.description: A colleague who signs in through the identity broker and uses applications.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Colleagues sign in to it from wherever they are, including their own devices at home.
external_entities.notes: The text does not specify whether colleagues are asked for a second factor.

external_entities.name: Franchise colleague
external_entities.description: A colleague from a franchise store whose own identity provider vouches for them.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Franchise colleagues do not have staff accounts with us; their own identity provider vouches for them

external_entities.name: Franchise store
external_entities.description: A franchise store whose colleagues are allowed to sign in through the identity broker.
external_entities.source_excerpt: We also let the franchise stores in.

external_entities.name: Franchise identity provider
external_entities.description: An identity provider that vouches for franchise colleagues and whose sign-in is accepted by the broker.
external_entities.source_excerpt: their own identity provider vouches for them and the broker takes that as a sign-in
external_entities.notes: The text does not specify which colleagues this provider is allowed to vouch for or where the provider runs.

external_entities.name: HR system
external_entities.description: The system from which the broker receives overnight changes to group membership and leaver status.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Group membership is not maintained there by hand — it comes from the HR system overnight.

processes.name: Identity broker
processes.description: Signs colleagues in, issues tokens, signs tokens, supplies public signing keys, and pulls identity changes from the HR system.
processes.source_excerpt: Everything colleagues use signs them in through one identity broker.
processes.notes: The broker keeps colleagues and their groups in its directory, and signs tokens with a signing key. The text does not specify the sign-in mechanism, token revocation mechanism beyond the stated twelve-hour lifetime, or second-factor use.

processes.name: Store admin console
processes.description: An application that lets a holder of a token containing the store-manager group change prices and void transactions for every store.
processes.source_excerpt: The store admin console is one of those applications.
processes.notes: The console does not check which store the colleague belongs to, so a store-manager token works against every store.

data_stores.name: Key store
data_stores.description: A store holding the signing key used by the broker for tokens issued to every application.
data_stores.source_excerpt: The broker signs tokens with a signing key it keeps in a key store.

data_stores.name: Directory
data_stores.description: The broker's directory containing colleagues and the groups they are in.
data_stores.source_excerpt: The broker keeps the colleagues and the groups they are in its own directory.
data_stores.notes: Group membership is populated from the HR system overnight. The text does not say whether the directory is encrypted where it sits.

data_stores.name: Audit log
data_stores.description: A log to which the broker writes sign-ins.
data_stores.source_excerpt: The broker writes sign-ins to an audit log.
data_stores.notes: Nobody has written down what the log records or whether it covers the franchise route. The text does not say whether the log is encrypted where it sits.

data_flows.name: sign in
data_flows.description: A colleague signs in to the identity broker.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Colleagues sign in to it from wherever they are

data_flows.name: issue token
data_flows.description: The identity broker issues a token containing the colleague's staff id and group list.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Once the broker has signed a colleague in it issues them a token.
data_flows.notes: The token is good for twelve hours and cannot be pulled back before it expires.
data_flows.data_description: A token carrying the colleague's staff id and a list of the groups they are in

data_flows.name: sign in
data_flows.description: A franchise colleague signs in through their own identity provider.
data_flows.source_excerpt: their own identity provider vouches for them

data_flows.name: vouch sign-in
data_flows.description: The franchise identity provider vouches for a franchise colleague and the broker accepts that as a sign-in.
data_flows.source_excerpt: their own identity provider vouches for them and the broker takes that as a sign-in
data_flows.notes: The text does not specify which colleagues the provider is allowed to vouch for.

data_flows.name: present token
data_flows.description: A colleague presents the issued token to the store admin console.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Every application takes that token and decides what the colleague may do from the groups in it.
data_flows.data_description: A token carrying the colleague's staff id and group list

data_flows.name: fetch public key
data_flows.description: The store admin console fetches the broker's public signing key to check token signatures.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Applications fetch the public half from the broker to check the signature.
data_flows.data_description: The public half of the token-signing key

data_flows.name: write signing key
data_flows.description: The identity broker keeps its signing key in the key store.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The broker signs tokens with a signing key it keeps in a key store.

data_flows.name: pull HR changes
data_flows.description: The identity broker pulls group-membership and leaver changes from the HR system once a night.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The broker pulls the changes once a night
data_flows.data_description: Group membership and colleague status changes

data_flows.name: update directory
data_flows.description: The identity broker updates its directory with colleagues and their groups.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The broker keeps the colleagues and the groups they are in its own directory.
data_flows.notes: The updates come from the HR system overnight.

data_flows.name: write sign-ins
data_flows.description: The identity broker writes sign-ins to the audit log.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The broker writes sign-ins to an audit log.
data_flows.notes: The text does not specify what the log records or whether it covers the franchise route.

trust_boundaries.name: Corporate network
trust_boundaries.description: The corporate network on which the identity broker and store admin console run.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: The broker runs on the corporate network.

trust_boundaries.name: Home devices
trust_boundaries.description: The home-device environment from which colleagues may sign in.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: including their own devices at home

trust_boundaries.name: Franchise stores
trust_boundaries.description: The franchise-store environment whose colleagues are allowed into the identity broker.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: We also let the franchise stores in.

assumptions.assumption: The key store's contents are confidential because it holds the broker's token-signing key.
assumptions.basis: The source states that the key store holds a signing key used to sign tokens.

assumptions.assumption: The directory's contents are confidential because it holds colleague records and group memberships.
assumptions.basis: The source states that the directory keeps colleagues and the groups they are in.

assumptions.assumption: The store admin console presents a web interface because the source names it as a console.
assumptions.basis: The procedure defines a console as a web interface.
